packageRules.description: Global safety: Wait 3 days before any automerge and require passing CI
Instant branch-based updates for ultra-low-risk internal maintenance
Group non-major updates and enable automerge
Route ALL major updates to a manual review

A rollback undoes a pin somebody chose on purpose, so it is never automerged. Renovate rolls back whenever the pinned version survives none of its own filters -- which minimumReleaseAge guarantees for any release pinned on the day it was cut, so the first-party bump below is the other half of this fix.

First-party releases are trusted the moment they exist. The soak period is there to let somebody else find the bad release first, and there is no somebody else for our own code -- while waiting means every fresh pin of our own tag is filtered out and rolled back.
Security engine bumps change what dragon detects, so a human reads the regression diff before they land

TypeScript is held below 7 while @hey-api/openapi-ts still needs 6. The generator reads the TypeScript compiler's internals, and they moved in 7: it dies with 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading AnyKeyword)', no SDK is produced, and the gate fails in every repository that generates a client from its OpenAPI document. Its peer range ends at 6 and no published release supports 7, so the upgrade cannot be taken by a person either -- an unheld major here is a pull request that can only ever be closed. Lift this as soon as a release supports 7; 6.x minors and patches keep flowing meanwhile.
